title: Gradient Backgrounds
slide_intent: Use tonal change to create depth while preserving a recognizable dominant hue.
strategic_value: Controlled magenta gradients can add spatial interest without weakening T-Mobile’s color identity.
demonstration: One large linear gradient is paired with smaller radial and freeform gradient specimens.
practical_value: Choose the gradient shape for the focal point and preserve the stated color distribution.

content_islands.name: Depth and distribution
content_islands.spec: Place gradient purpose, light-source guidance and 80/20 rule at left.

content_islands.name: Gradient comparison
content_islands.spec: Show a large linear example alongside stacked radial and freeform examples with labels.

ingredient.name: Magenta gradient
ingredient.role: Create depth and focus within a recognizable brand-color field.
ingredient.application: Use approved gradients with an 80/20 split so magenta covers 80%; use the lightest point to establish the light source.
ingredient.scope: Gradient applications in the February 2024 guide. The 80% instruction does not establish a ratio for every non-gradient page or for a whole campaign.

reference_purposes.Intent: The explanatory copy connects gradients to depth, focus and the illusion of space on a flat surface.
reference_purposes.Expression: Linear, radial and freeform specimens demonstrate three distinct ways to distribute light within magenta.
reference_purposes.Application: The page uses the lightest point to locate the light source and specifies an 80/20 distribution for gradient compositions.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Magenta must have 80% coverage in the described gradient applications, and only approved branded gradients may be used.
